behaviour: Unit tests for the range model, line mapping across wrapping, bound containers and font changes, run layout, and undo/redo of a range change through the element delta.
rules: 1. Import the range functions from "../src/textStyleRanges", getTextStyleRunLayout and getBoundTextMaxWidth from "../src/textElement", wrapText from "../src/textWrapping", setCustomTextMetricsProvider from "../src/textMeasurements", ElementsDelta from "../src/delta", newElementWith from "../src/mutateElement", API from "@excalidraw/excalidraw/tests/helpers/api", arrayToMap from "@excalidraw/common", and the types FontString, SceneElementsMap, FractionalIndex and ExcalidrawTextElement from "../src/types".
2. Use `const font = "10px Cascadia, Segoe UI Emoji" as FontString` (10px per character in tests), and the sample text "Bid request timeout 120ms", in which "120ms" is [20, 25).
3. The font-change cases install `setCustomTextMetricsProvider({ getLineWidth: (text, f) => text.length * parseFloat(f) })` and reset it with setCustomTextMetricsProvider(undefined) in afterEach.

4. The delta cases apply deltas as packages/element/tests/delta.test.tsx does: applyTo(map, map, { excludedProperties: new Set(["version", "versionNonce"]) }), on maps of a text element created with an index.

tests.name: normalizeStyleRanges clamps, drops empty or colourless ranges and sorts
tests.given: ranges [{start:8,end:99,strokeColor:'#f00'},{start:2,end:2,strokeColor:'#0f0'},{start:-3,end:2,backgroundColor:'#ff0'},{start:4,end:6}] for textLength 10
tests.expect: [{start:0,end:2,backgroundColor:'#ff0'},{start:8,end:10,strokeColor:'#f00'}]

tests.name: normalizeStyleRanges merges adjacent and overlapping same-style ranges
tests.expect: [{start:0,end:8,strokeColor:red}]

tests.name: normalizeStyleRanges lets later entries win inside an overlap
tests.given: [{0,6,strokeColor:red},{3,9,strokeColor:blue}] for textLength 10

tests.name: normalizeStyleRanges returns undefined when nothing remains
tests.given: undefined, [] and [{start:1,end:1,strokeColor:red}]
tests.expect: undefined for each

tests.name: applyStyleToRange over part of a range splits it
tests.given: ranges [{0,10,strokeColor:red}], applying {strokeColor:blue} to [3,6) with textLength 10 and base '#1e1e1e'

tests.name: applyStyleToRange keeps the other property and fills gaps
tests.given: ranges [{2,4,strokeColor:red}], applying {backgroundColor:yellow} to [0,6)
tests.expect: [{0,2,bg yellow},{2,4,red + bg yellow},{4,6,bg yellow}]

tests.name: applyStyleToRange clears with the base colour or transparent
tests.given: ranges [{0,5,strokeColor:red,backgroundColor:yellow}], applying {strokeColor:'#1e1e1e'} with base '#1e1e1e', then {backgroundColor:'transparent'}
tests.expect: first [{0,5,backgroundColor:yellow}], then undefined

tests.name: shiftStyleRangesForEdit on insert before, inside and after a range
tests.given: range [{4,7,red}] on 'abcdefghij'; insert 'XY' at 0, at 5, and at 9

tests.name: shiftStyleRangesForEdit does not colour text typed at a range's edges
tests.given: range [{4,7,red}] on 'abcdefghij'; insert 'X' at 4, then (separately) at 7

tests.name: shiftStyleRangesForEdit on delete before, overlapping and inside
tests.given: range [{4,7,red}] on 'abcdefghij'; delete [0,2), delete [3,5), delete [5,6)

tests.name: deleting a range's text entirely drops it

tests.name: shiftStyleRangesForEdit uses the caret to place an ambiguous insertion
tests.given: range [{0,2,red}] on 'aa'; next text 'aaa' with caret 1 and with caret 3

tests.name: getStyleRunsForLines splits a single line into runs
tests.given: originalText 'Bid request timeout 120ms', the same text as wrappedText, range [{20,25,red}]
tests.expect: [[{text:'Bid request timeout '},{text:'120ms',strokeColor:red}]]

tests.name: getStyleRunsForLines follows soft wraps and trimmed spaces
tests.given: the sample text wrapped with wrapText(text, font, 100), range [{12,25,red}] covering 'timeout 120ms'
tests.expect: each line's runs concatenate to the line; the run texts carrying red concatenate to 'timeout120ms'; the 'Bid' and 'request' lines have no coloured run

tests.name: getStyleRunsForLines keeps hard line breaks and empty lines aligned
tests.given: originalText 'ab\n\ncd' (wrapped text identical), range [{4,5,red}]
tests.expect: [[{text:'ab'}],[],[{text:'c',strokeColor:red},{text:'d'}]]

tests.name: runs survive a bound-text container's wrapping
tests.given: a rectangle of width 120 and a bound text with the sample text and range [{20,25,red}], wrapped with wrapText(originalText, font, getBoundTextMaxWidth(container, text))

tests.name: runs survive a font change that re-wraps the same text
tests.given: the font-size-scaled metrics provider; the sample text wrapped at maxWidth 200 with a 10px font and with a 20px font, range [{20,25,red}]
tests.expect: the two wraps differ in line count, and in both the coloured runs concatenate to '120ms'

tests.given: a text 'hello world' of width 200 with range [{6,11,red}], textAlign left, then center

tests.name: undo restores the previous ranges and redo re-applies them

tests.expect: delta.inverse() applied to after gives styleRanges undefined; delta applied to before gives [{0,4,red}]; both report a visible change

tests.expect: the calculated delta's updated entry has no styleRanges key

behaviour: jsdom tests: with a textarea selection, the colour actions apply to the range and keep the editor open; typing shifts the range; a collapsed selection colours the whole element.
rules: 1. The new describe renders <Excalidraw handleKeyboardGlobally={true} /> in beforeEach, sets one text element 'Bid request timeout 120ms' with strokeColor '#1e1e1e', selects it and presses Enter. It then reads the editor with getTextEditor().
2. Picks run as act(() => h.app.actionManager.executeAction(actionChangeStrokeColor, "ui", { color })) and likewise for actionChangeBackgroundColor.

3. The selection is set with editor.setSelectionRange(start, end) before a pick. For typing, set editor.value, then setSelectionRange(caret, caret), then fireEvent.input(editor), so the caret hint matches the edit.

tests.name: applies a stroke colour to the selected range only
tests.given: selection [20,25), stroke pick '#e03131'
tests.expect: styleRanges equals [{start:20,end:25,strokeColor:'#e03131'}]; the element's strokeColor is still '#1e1e1e'; h.state.editingTextElement is still the text; editor.selectionStart/End are still 20/25

tests.name: applies a background colour as a highlight on the range
tests.given: selection [20,25), stroke pick '#e03131', then background pick '#ffec99'
tests.expect: styleRanges equals [{start:20,end:25,strokeColor:'#e03131',backgroundColor:'#ffec99'}]; the element's backgroundColor is unchanged

tests.name: typing before the range shifts it
tests.given: a range [20,25) applied; then the editor value is set to 'X' plus the old value with caret 1, and an input event is fired
tests.expect: styleRanges equals [{start:21,end:26,strokeColor:'#e03131'}]

tests.name: typing inside the range grows it
tests.given: a range [20,25) applied; then '0' is inserted at offset 22 with caret 23, and an input event is fired
tests.expect: styleRanges equals [{start:20,end:26,strokeColor:'#e03131'}]

tests.name: with a collapsed selection the pick colours the whole element
tests.given: selection [5,5), stroke pick '#e03131'
tests.expect: the element's strokeColor is '#e03131' and it has no styleRanges

tests.name: with the whole text selected the pick colours the whole element
tests.given: selection [0,25) (all of 'Bid request timeout 120ms'), stroke pick '#e03131'
tests.expect: the element's strokeColor is '#e03131' and it has no styleRanges

tests.name: ranges survive leaving the editor
tests.given: a range [20,25) applied, then Keyboard.exitTextEditor(editor)
tests.expect: the element still has styleRanges [{start:20,end:25,strokeColor:'#e03131'}] and originalText is unchanged

behaviour: Export tests: SVG <tspan> runs and highlight <rect>s, dark-mode filtering of run colours, no <tspan> without ranges, and canvas per-run fillStyle and highlight fillRect.
rules: 1. Fixture: `{ ...API.createElement({ type: "text", text: "foo bar baz", strokeColor: "#1e1e1e", fontSize: 20 }), styleRanges: [{ start: 0, end: 3, strokeColor: "#e03131" }, { start: 4, end: 7, backgroundColor: "#ffec99" }] }`, with textAlign left. In tests each character measures 10px.

2. SVG cases use exportScene({ type: "svg", data: { elements: [text] }, config: { canvasBackgroundColor: false } }). Read <text>, <tspan> and <rect> through querySelectorAll on the result's [data-id] group or the whole svg.
3. The canvas case uses exportScene({ type: "canvas", data: { elements: [text], files: null } }) and reads (canvas.getContext("2d") as any).__getEvents().

tests.name: exports one tspan per run with its own fill
tests.given: the fixture exported to SVG
tests.expect: one <text>, whose tspans have texts ['foo',' ','bar',' baz'] and fills ['#e03131','#1e1e1e','#1e1e1e','#1e1e1e']; the <text> keeps x, y, font-family, font-size, text-anchor, direction and dominant-baseline

tests.name: exports a highlight rect behind the background run
tests.given: the fixture exported to SVG
tests.expect: exactly one rect with fill '#ffec99' inside the text's group, with x 40, y 0, width 30 and height fontSize * lineHeight

tests.name: filters run colours in dark mode
tests.given: the fixture exported to SVG with config.theme THEME.DARK
tests.expect: the 'foo' tspan fill is applyDarkModeFilter('#e03131'), the other tspans use applyDarkModeFilter('#1e1e1e') and the highlight rect fill is applyDarkModeFilter('#ffec99')

tests.name: exports a text without ranges with no tspan
tests.given: the same text without styleRanges
tests.expect: no tspan in the svg, and the <text> textContent is 'foo bar baz'

tests.name: draws runs on canvas with their own fillStyle and a highlight
tests.given: the fixture exported to canvas
tests.expect: a fillRect event of width 30 with fillStyle '#ffec99' set before it; fillText events for 'foo', ' ', 'bar' and ' baz'; the fillStyle set before 'foo' is '#e03131' and before 'bar' is '#1e1e1e'
